# AirFRANS: the first industrial benchmark {#sec-airfrans}

::: {.callout-important title="Read this before any number in this chapter: the protocol was contaminated"}
**Every comparative result below is development-set performance, not
confirmatory.** The external review's P0 finding (2026-07-17,
CONFIRMED in source): this chapter's campaign carved its validation
set out of AirFRANS's **official test split** —
`validation_names = test_names[:MAX_VALIDATION_CASES]` — so best
checkpoints were selected on test members, and the wider iteration
loop used official-test results to steer architecture choices. The
ladder's *internal* comparisons (arm vs arm, all trained and scored
identically) are much less affected than the *external* ones; but
every ranking against a published baseline in this chapter — "front
of the baseline pack", "second only to GLOBE", "beats every
published model 5–8×" — is a number a model was allowed to peek at.

The remediation is registered and partly executed:

- **(a) Done.** Validation is now carved from training cases only,
  under a fixed protocol seed (commit `85dcf939`; the old form is
  documented in-source at `datasets/airfrans_train.py:1210`).
- **(b) Partly done.** Headline arms re-ran under the frozen clean
  protocol (12/12 lanes, @sec-nb-b22-verdict). First read: the
  chapter's *recommended* arm `mt_nl_members_log` is tight and
  healthy across seeds ($u_x$ 0.0145 / 0.0145 / 0.0159, surface
  $C_p \approx 0.007$) and lands **inside** the old development-set
  range — so the V4 log-radial rung and the surface-pressure story
  look protocol-robust. Two things did not survive cleanly: the
  `members` arm shows an outlier seed ($u_x$ 0.0657 vs 0.020/0.024),
  and **the `pseudo` arm's surface pressure collapsed to
  mean-predictor level (z-score 1.0–1.5) on all three clean seeds.**
- **(c) Not done.** The AoA-extrapolation windfall — this chapter's
  sharpest claim, and one carried by exactly the `pseudo` arm that
  just collapsed in-distribution — has **not** been re-evaluated on
  clean checkpoints. The extrapolation (`evalx`) leg is unrun. Until
  it runs, that claim is suspended, not merely caveated.

Unchanged by any of this: **GLOBE remains 16–30× ahead of us on
surface pressure** (≈18× in the clean read), which was already
conceded throughout. Pre-registered odds that the chapter's headline
claims survive the clean protocol: **~60%** (@sec-nb-checkin-2).

The pre-registration sections below (hypotheses, arms, protocol) are
preserved exactly as written before any training run — they are the
record against which @sec-airfrans-results reports, and they are
unaffected by the defect.
:::

## Why AirFRANS, and why now

The program's benchmarks so far pose exact-label or solver-labeled
problems that we designed ourselves. AirFRANS (Bonnet et al., NeurIPS
2022, arXiv [2212.07564](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.07564)) is the
first *external* benchmark: 1,000 cases of steady incompressible
RANS (OpenFOAM, eddy-viscosity closure) over NACA airfoils spanning
Reynolds numbers of 2–6 million and angles of attack from $-5°$ to
$+15°$, with volume fields (velocity, pressure, turbulent viscosity) at
roughly 180k mesh points per case. It fits the program's scope exactly:
a steady, homogeneous PDE system, driven entirely from the boundary (an
airfoil with a no-slip label plus a freestream), with no interior
forcing and no interior data at the query points — and the governing
equations are genuinely not knowable, because the turbulence closure is
an empirical model, not a derived operator.

Two further reasons make it the *right* first industrial benchmark:

1. **It is the rare public dataset whose boundary-value problem is
   actually recoverable.** The freestream and no-slip conditions are
   explicit, the label pathologies are small and characterizable
   (energy-conservation violations at 0.003% of points; near-wall
   pressure-gradient artifacts), and the working constants
   ($\rho = 1$, $\nu = 1.56\times10^{-5}$ m²/s) can be verified from
   the data itself.
2. **It is GLOBE's flagship result.** The `MeshTransformer` exists to
   generalize GLOBE (arXiv
   [2511.15856](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15856)) — keep its theory
   (similarity equivariance, boundary-integral information flow,
   nondimensionalization), replace its bespoke machinery with
   transformer-native simplicity. GLOBE's published AirFRANS numbers
   (roughly 200× lower z-score MSE than the dataset's four reference
   baselines on the full split; 7–70× below the strongest newer
   surrogates on the scarce split, at 117k parameters) are therefore
   the direct test of the program's founding bet: *does the
   simplification retain the family's advantage?*

One honest framing note, stated before any result: 2D airfoil RANS is
classically solvable — integral-boundary-layer codes deliver
XFOIL-quality answers in milliseconds on a CPU. AirFRANS is a
*benchmark with unusually good labels*, never the use case. The use
case remains the 3D configurations of @sec-drivaerml, where no XFOIL
exists.

## The mapping, in this program's terms

AirFRANS poses precisely the mapping this program learns:

$$
\{\underbrace{\text{airfoil boundary}}_{\text{no-slip, geometry only}},\
\underbrace{\hat U_\infty}_{\text{global drive vector}},\
\underbrace{\ln \mathrm{Re}_c}_{\text{global operator scalar}}\}
\;\longmapsto\;
\{\Delta U/|U_\infty|,\ C_p,\ \ln(1+\nu_t/\nu)\}
\ \text{at interior query points.}
$$

Three declared representation choices, each with a first-principles
license:

- **The freestream enters as a global drive direction, and the model
  predicts the disturbance field** $\Delta U = U - U_\infty$. The
  additive freestream baseline is exact structure (it is the solution
  at infinite distance), and the disturbance decays — which is what the
  far-field machinery of @sec-farfield-ladder was built for.
- **Reynolds number enters as one dimensionless global scalar**,
  $\ln\mathrm{Re}_c$ — scalars condition kernels freely without
  breaking equivariance (@sec-pde-theory). This replaces GLOBE's
  two-reference-length construction (chord plus viscous scale
  $\delta_{FS} = \sqrt{\nu c/|U_\infty|}$, whose log-ratio is
  $\tfrac12\ln\mathrm{Re}_c$) with the intrinsic gauge plus one scalar:
  the same information, less machinery — itself a parsimony test.
- **The monopole-free deflation stays OFF.** A lifting airfoil carries
  net circulation — exactly the topological sector that knob
  structurally kills (@sec-farfield-ladder). Its physics license does
  not hold here, so the contract is not declared.

## Pre-registered hypotheses and arms

All arms use the reference configuration (one encoder layer, one
full-width head, two exact kernel members) in
`field_mode="zero_preserving_nonlinear"` — RANS is nonlinear, so
drive-linearity is not declared. The arms:

| arm | adds | tests |
|---|---|---|
| `mt_nl` | — (baseline) | the plain architecture on industrial RANS |
| `mt_nl_pseudo` | 2D pseudoscalar (`0o`) sector | **H2**: lift/circulation is handed content |
| `mt_nl_decay` | `decaying_direct_drive` | **H3**: exterior far-field structure transfers |

- **H1 (baseline competence).** `mt_nl` beats all four AirFRANS
  reference baselines (MLP, GraphSAGE, PointNet, Graph U-Net) on all
  four published z-score metrics of the scarce task. *Falsifier: worse
  than the best of the four on any metric.*
- **H2 (parity contract).** A lifting flow at angle of attack is
  handed: reflecting the geometry and freestream flips the sign of
  circulation and lift. The measured parity floor and its `0o` break
  (@sec-fluid-suites) predict the pseudo arm improves lift-linked
  content specifically. *Falsifier: no improvement of `mt_nl_pseudo`
  over `mt_nl` outside seed noise at 5 seeds.*
- **H3 (far-field structure).** The decay-envelope contract closed the
  far-field ladder on exact-label suites (0.694 → 0.090,
  @sec-farfield-ladder); AirFRANS's exterior domain is its first
  solver-labeled test. *Falsifier: `mt_nl_decay` no better than
  `mt_nl` on far-from-body error bands.*
- **Family acceptance (the head-to-head).** At matched training budget
  and matched inputs, the best arm lands within **2×** of GLOBE's
  published scarce-split z-score MSE on velocity and pressure —
  supporting "the transformer-native simplification retains the
  family's advantage." *Refutation condition, reported as first-class
  if hit: worse than GLOBE by more than 5× on any headline metric,
  which would mean GLOBE's bespoke machinery (hyperlayers, Padé
  kernels, multi-scale expansion) is load-bearing, not removable.*
- **Stretch (pre-registered, exploratory).** GLOBE's one partial loss
  is AoA-extrapolation volume pressure (11.38×10⁻², tied with the
  dataset baselines). Whether declared contracts help a global
  flow-topology shift is a genuine coin-flip; we record the prediction
  "parity typing helps AoA asymmetry" and will report either outcome.
- **H4 (declared viscous scale — added 2026-07-05 after the banded
  diagnostic, before the arm was built).** The pilot's error is
  wall-concentrated: 49% of velocity MSE inside $d/c < 10^{-4}$ (12.5%
  of points; profile replicated across seeds and arms). The boundary
  layer lives at $\delta/c \sim \mathrm{Re}^{-1/2} \approx
  5\times10^{-4}$, a scale our kernels only see through scalar
  conditioning of a chord-scale radial argument. H4 declares it: an
  auxiliary per-problem length scale ($\mathrm{Re}^{-1/2}$ times the
  gauge, similarity-covariant by construction) entering the pair
  kernels as additional $r/\delta$-normalized invariants.
  One structural fact sharpens the design (noted before building): the
  singpair reference arm has *no learned pair-radial pathway* — its
  only $r$-dependence is the two exact singular members, so there is
  no carrier for a boundary-layer-scale profile even in principle. The
  H4 arm therefore adds smooth MLP members fed by the
  $r/\delta$-scaled invariants, and the experiment carries a
  **capacity control**: identical MLP members *without* the auxiliary
  scale. *Pre-registered acceptance: the aux-scale arm reduces band-0
  velocity MSE ≥2× vs both the singpair baseline AND the
  plain-members control at 3 seeds under protocol-v1, without outer-band
  regression. Falsifiers: control ≈ aux-scale (capacity, not
  declaration, was the deficit) or no band-0 movement at all (deficit
  is supervision/optimization, not kernel scale).*

## Protocol

- **Tasks, in order:** `scarce` (200 train / 200 test; cheapest, most
  decorated comparison surface), then `full` (800/200), then the
  official `reynolds` and `aoa` extrapolation tasks evaluated from the
  full-trained arms.
- **Metrics:** z-score-normalized MSE per field, matching the AirFRANS
  reference implementation exactly (for direct comparability with the
  published table: the four dataset baselines, GLOBE, Transolver,
  MARIO, enf2enf), *plus* physically nondimensionalized MAE
  (velocity/|U∞|, C_p), which we regard as the more honest unit and
  report alongside.
- **Loss:** Huber, matching GLOBE's declared choice (robust to the
  dataset's known label artifacts); stated here so it is not a
  post-hoc degree of freedom.
- **Schedule (protocol-v1, adopted 2026-07-05 after the flat-LR
  pilot, before any v1 run):** cosine from GLOBE's scaled peak
  ($10^{-3}\sqrt{\text{queries}/2048} = 1.41\times10^{-3}$ at 4,096)
  to peak/64, GLOBE's endpoints. Disclosure: GLOBE's own scheduler is
  ReduceLROnPlateau between the same endpoints; we use the
  deterministic cosine so no validation-coupled control flow enters
  the protocol, and record the difference in every run report. The
  flat-LR pilot (protocol-v0) is retained as exploration, reported
  separately.
- **Sampling:** full airfoil boundary every step (no boundary
  downsampling); 4,096 volume query points per iteration
  (GLOBE-matched).
- **Label hygiene:** energy-conservation violations ($C_{pt} > 1.02$,
  ~0.003% of points) are excluded identically from training and
  evaluation of every arm, and $\rho = 1$ (the verified value, not the
  mislabeled 1.204). **Protocol amendment, 2026-07-05 (pre-training,
  before any run):** this section originally also excluded
  $|\nabla C_p \cdot c| > 20$ rows. The first conversion pass measured
  that screen deleting 16–23% of each case's points, concentrated in
  exactly the near-wall region — it is a *gradient-target* hygiene rule
  in GLOBE's pipeline (a target we do not predict), not a row exclusion.
  The screen is now recorded per case as a diagnostic count only. No
  model was trained under the earlier text; the amendment is logged in
  the notebook.
- **Seeds:** 3 per arm during the campaign; 5 for any load-bearing
  claim, per the program's standing rule.
- **Compute:** single-GPU per seed (the airfoil boundary is ~10³
  segments — far below the dense-decode wall), seeds packed 4-per-node
  on B200 nodes.

## Results {#sec-airfrans-results}

The campaign resolved as a **mechanism ladder**: five rungs, each a
pre-registered hypothesis with a falsifier, each verdict logged in the
notebook before the next rung was designed. The headline: from
~600× behind GLOBE at the pilot to the front of the published
baseline pack on velocity and second-only-to-GLOBE on surface
pressure — with every gain attributed to a named mechanism, not
tuning.

### The ladder at a glance

| rung | mechanism | verdict | u_x effect | notebook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| schedule | GLOBE-endpoint cosine | adopted | ~13% | @sec-nb-airfrans-v1 |
| H2 parity | 2D pseudoscalar sector | **confirmed** (4 seeds, no overlap) | ~15% + AoA windfall | @sec-nb-airfrans-v1 |
| H3 far-field | $r^{-2}$ decay envelope | **refuted** — wakes don't decay like point singularities | −20% (worse) | @sec-nb-airfrans-v1 |
| H4 members | smooth MLP members (capacity control **beat** the declared viscous scale) | control wins 6× | 6× | @sec-nb-h4-verdict |
| V4 log-radial | $\ln$, $/\!\sqrt{\cdot}$ pair features | **confirmed** | 1.66× | @sec-nb-v-verdicts |

H3 is the chapter's honest negative: the decay contract that closed
the exact-label far-field ladder is *exactly enforced and exactly
wrong* for a wake-shedding airfoil. H4's verdict is the program's
strongest parsimony datum: the pre-registered capacity control
(members *without* the declared viscous scale) beat the declared-scale
arm ~6× — the deficit was a missing learned pair-radial pathway, not a
missing declaration.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

::: {.callout-warning title="Development-set table"}
Every column comparison in this table is against published numbers
under the contaminated protocol described at the top of the chapter.
Read it as *where the mechanisms got us*, not as a ranking. The

Standing (development-set): velocity at the front of the baseline pack (tied with
GraphSAGE within seed noise — H1's velocity clause reads "tied," not
"met"); volume pressure ~8× past every baseline, within ~2× of MARIO;
**surface pressure 3–4× better than MARIO**, second only to GLOBE.
The family-acceptance bar (≤2× GLOBE) is not met on velocity; the
refutation condition (>5× worse with bespoke machinery load-bearing)
is also not the story — the gap closed 600× → ~40× by removable
mechanisms and continues to close.

### V4: learned log-radial scales, the largest single rung

`mt_nl_members_log` replaces nothing and declares nothing — it feeds
the member MLPs log-radial pair features
($\ln(a{+}\epsilon)$, $b/\sqrt{a{+}\epsilon}$,
$v\!\cdot\!r/\sqrt{a{+}\epsilon}$) that make power-law scales
*linearly learnable*. Pooled convention, test split, clean seeds
(anomalous seeds reported separately below, nothing silently
excluded):

| arm | seeds (clean) | u_x median | vs members-8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mt_nl_members` (protocol LR) | 5/5 clean | 0.0213 | — |
| `mt_nl_members_log` | 4/5 clean | **0.0128** | **1.66×** |

This is the H4-L thesis vindicated in its learnable form
(@sec-nb-v-verdicts): the viscous scale the H4 declaration tried to
*inject* is better *learned* — the same conclusion twice, by
different routes.

**V5 (subsumption, a simplifying null):** composing log-radial
features with the parity-composition arm
(`mt_nl_members_log_pseudo`, 3/3 seeds: 0.0135–0.0155) adds nothing
over `members_log` alone. The pseudo-composition's earlier ~30% gain
and the log-features' gain were the *same missing capability*
(power-law radial structure); the feature-level carrier is cheaper.
**Recommended arm going forward: `mt_nl_members_log`.**

**LR ladder (V3 coda):** halving LR costs medians monotonically
(protocol 0.0213 → 5×10⁻⁴: 0.0246 → 2.5×10⁻⁴: 0.0356) — but see the
anomaly census below for what lower LR *buys*.

### The AoA-extrapolation windfall (pre-registered stretch)

::: {.callout-important title="This claim is SUSPENDED pending the clean re-run"}
This section reports the campaign's sharpest single result, and it is
the one most exposed by the protocol defect — it rests on the
`pseudo` arm, whose in-distribution surface pressure **collapsed to
mean-predictor level on all three clean-protocol seeds**. The
extrapolation evaluation has not been re-run on clean checkpoints
(remediation leg (c), unrun). The mechanism argument below — a
within-program control isolating the parity sector — is the part
most likely to survive, because it is an internal comparison; the
5–8× margin against published models is the part least likely to.
Treat the numbers as development-set until `evalx` reruns.
:::

The chapter's pre-registered coin-flip ("parity typing helps AoA
asymmetry") resolved as the campaign's sharpest single result
(@sec-nb-extrapolation): zero-shot AoA-extrapolation volume pressure,
official protocol, 3 seeds — `mt_nl_pseudo` **0.0134–0.0214** vs
GLOBE's published **0.1138** (its one weakness, where it ties the
Bonnet baselines). The parity-typed arm beats *every published model
5–8×* on exactly the metric where the flow's handedness shifts
hardest, and the within-program control (`mt_nl`, no parity sector:
0.024–0.048) pins the mechanism to the sector, not the architecture.

The members-class extrapolation evals have now landed
(@sec-nb-probes-verdict; GLOBE per-sample convention, official
held-out `reynolds` and `aoa` splits, zero-shot from scarce-trained
checkpoints; provenance: evalx jobs 5048837/5048838,
`output/airfrans_evalx`, HSG), and they extend the story from
pressure to **velocity**:

| arm (clean seeds) | u_x, Re-extrap | u_x, AoA-extrap | u_x, in-dist |
|---|---|---|---|
| singpair-class (`mt_nl`) | 0.118–0.122 | 0.119–0.123 | — |
| `mt_nl_members_log` | **0.0147–0.0190** | **0.0208–0.0268** | 0.0128 |
| `mt_nl_members_wide` | 0.0159–0.0224 (4/5) | 0.0212–0.0297 | — |

The recommended arm (`members_log`) **extrapolates to within
~1.2–2× of its own in-distribution accuracy** on both official
axes, where singpair-class arms degrade ~10×. One honest asterisk:
`members_wide` seed 17 blows up on the Reynolds split (u_x 0.101)
while clean in-distribution — the tail-anomaly signature (see the
tail section below) surfacing under extrapolation stress; the census
discipline (≥5 seeds, report all) is what catches it. Convention
and split caveats as above: per-sample GLOBE convention, official
extrapolation protocol, no fine-tuning.

### The surface-task probe (T1-reduced)

A surface-only companion task (queries = airfoil panel centroids)
tested whether the exterior-trace correction that bought 2× on
DrivAerML (@sec-drivaerml) transfers to 2D. Verdict
(@sec-nb-t1-verdict): **weak support, not confirmation** — trace wins
4/5 seeds under both metric conventions but only by 1.2–1.35× in the
median, within the arm-internal seed spread. The synthesis, consistent
across both datasets: the trace defect is a *learnable-but-slow bias*
— absorbable where budget and problem size allow (2D, 1000 epochs),
worth 2× where they don't (3D, 500 epochs). Trace mode stays on
everywhere: it is exact and costs nothing.

### The tail anomaly: LR-gated, deterministic, and partly load-bearing

Across all protocol-LR member-class arms, a minority of seeds blow up
in a *single velocity field* while other fields stay clean. The
census (@sec-nb-v-verdicts): members-8 0/5, members_log 1/5,
members16 1/3, members32 1/3, members_wide 0/5, LR-halved 1/5,
LR-quartered **0/5**. Three facts now pin the mechanism
(@sec-nb-tail-verdict):

1. **Deterministic given seed.** An accidental exact replication
   (a no-op LR override — logged as a design error) reproduced the
   anomalous seed's blowup to four significant digits. Not a
   transient, not hardware: it is baked into the (init, data-order)
   draw.
2. **LR-gated.** The corrected deciding experiment (`members_log`
   seeds 17–21 at base 7.07×10⁻⁴ = 0.71× protocol) delivered the
   pre-registered prediction exactly: **0/5 anomalies**, with the
   protocol-anomalous seed dropping from u_x 0.100 to a clean 0.0156.
3. **The edge is partly where the performance lives.** The backoff
   cost 22% in clean-seed median (0.0156 vs 0.0128), exceeding the
   pre-registered ≤15% bound — the falsifier's trade-off branch.

Verdict: an LR × member-capacity edge-of-stability interaction,
confirmed in its anomaly prediction, refused in its free-lunch
clause. Practical recommendation: run member-class arms at protocol
LR with ≥5 seeds and report the census — anomalies are single-field,
detectable, and seed-pinned — rather than paying 22% median for
their absence. Width appears stabilizing (wide 0/5) while flattening
destabilizes (16/32 at 1/3 each) at fixed LR; that interaction is
open.
